model.rationale: DelBene combines a fifteen-point district lean with a roughly 400-to-1 financial advantage over an opponent who has raised under $9,000, and no outside money has entered against her. Markets and fundamentals alike point to an easy incumbent win, so the only uncertainty is the exact size of the margin.
model.watch: With no public polling of this race, a late independent survey or unexpected outside spending on either side would be the first sign the margin is moving.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzan DelBene enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by fifteen points on the partisan baseline. She has raised about $3.55 million this cycle and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Republican Mary Silva has reported roughly $8,400 in contributions and about $1,200 in cash. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent, and no public polling of the race has been conducted. Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 98 percent.

DelBene has held the seat since 2012, and the district's fundamentals combined with the stark disparity in campaign resources leave the challenger with little visible path. A substantially different result would require forces not currently visible in the record.
